claims.label: FAO meat supply per person, 2023
claims.text: Tonga had the highest meat supply per person in 2023: about 157 kg per person per year (156.93), the top of 176 countries in the dataset.
claims.note: Rank from data/meat_supply_per_person_2023.csv (all 176 entities with an ISO code, 2023). 156.93/365 = 0.43 kg a day.

claims.label: FAO meat supply per person, 2023
claims.text: Mongolia was second in 2023 with about 136 kg per person.

claims.label: FAO meat supply per person, 2023
claims.text: The Marshall Islands were third in 2023 with about 126 kg per person.

claims.label: FAO meat supply per person, 2023
claims.text: The United States was fourth in 2023 with about 122 kg per person.

claims.label: FAO meat supply per person, 2023
claims.text: India had about 8 kg of meat per person in 2023.

claims.label: FAO meat supply per person, 2023
claims.text: The Democratic Republic of Congo had the lowest figure in 2023, about 3.5 kg per person (under four).
The figure is meat available for consumption (supply), not meat eaten: it does not correct for waste, so actual consumption may be lower; it excludes fish and seafood.
claims.quote: Quantity that is available for consumption at the end of the supply chain. It does not account for consumer waste, so the quantity that is actually consumed may be lower; Data excludes fish and other seafood sources

myths.myth: Americans eat the most meat in the world.
myths.truth: In FAO's 2023 supply data the US is fourth, behind Tonga, Mongolia and the Marshall Islands.
